items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: never did I met him many times but I don't know him now really

ctx.x: I'm sure that we've begun to get into a marsh of questions here beyond the scope of common understanding and when you talk about the musician being a critic this is only where the musician can tread with safety is in these matters of the tempered scale and understanding of these slight shadings

when I was saying for instance that Chicago pianists weren't much good I realized that I was being a little presumptuous really there were some wonderful pianists I mean Art Grunewald that we were talking about was of course really first class in many ways Roy Bargy there were some very very good pianist around but Chicago music as such was not distinguished for its piano I think the first piano that anybody ever heard of was Heinz who may possibly be the greatest one that ever lived
when did you get to know Heinz
